title: Where it grows
subtitle: The Pyrenees and the River Plate
objectives: Compare the climates of both homes

steps.title: Madiran
steps.body: Tannat's French home is Madiran, in Gascony, close to the Pyrenees. Madiran must be at least 60% Tannat, often blended with Cabernet Franc, Cabernet Sauvignon or Fer Servadou. The climate is mild and fairly wet, with Atlantic influence. Tannat also appears in Irouléguy, in the Basque Country, and in Saint-Mont.

steps.title: Uruguay
steps.body: Basque immigrants brought Tannat to Uruguay in the 1870s; one of them, Pascual Harriague, gave it its early local name, Harriague. Today it is Uruguay's national grape, about a quarter of the vineyard. Uruguay's humid, maritime climate on the River Plate and the Atlantic gives Tannat riper, rounder tannins than in Madiran.

steps.prompt: Match each place to its Tannat connection.
steps.explanation: Tannat travelled from the Basque Country to South America with emigrants.

steps.title: Similar yet different
steps.body: Both homes are humid, with rain during the growing season, unlike the dry Andes. Growers must fight disease. Uruguay is warmer and gets more sun, so Tannat ripens more fully. Canelones, near Montevideo, makes most of it; Maldonado, near the sea, and Rivera, in the north, give new styles.

steps.prompt: Why is Tannat from Uruguay often softer than Madiran?
options: It is made from different grapes
Uruguay's warmer, sunnier climate ripens the tannins more
It is blended with white wine
steps.explanation: More warmth and sun bring riper, rounder tannins.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Madiran, near the Pyrenees, is Tannat's French home
Basque immigrants took it to Uruguay in the 1870s
Uruguay's warmer climate gives softer, riper Tannat
